transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 3:00 PM PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Stellaris AI, CTO), Mark Davies (Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary: quick discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart — goal is to evaluate hosted vs dedicated for latency/cost tradeoffs, time-to-first-token, and security requirements for pilot. Client interested in free credits and a fast POC.

Topics: quickstart flow, free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated/private, SOC2/KMS/SSO, benchmarking plan, next steps

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya with Redwood, AE on this account. Samir from our SE team is with me.
[00:08] Samir Patel: Hey all. happy to dig into the tech details, latency profiles, and how quick the quickstart is.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, Samir. thanks. We are looking to evaluate Redwood for a customer-facing assistant we want to ship this quarter — main concerns are latency for short chat flows and cost at scale.
[00:30] Mark Davies: yeah, and also our infra preference — we currently run on EKS and have a VPC-first policy. curious about private deployment vs hosted.
[00:40] Priya Singh: I'm mostly here for security questions — data retention, KMS, audit logs, and SSO.
[00:48] Maya Chen: Great — high level: Redwood has a PLG quickstart that is self-serve. you can get an org, free credits, and hit first token in under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart. We'll walk through the flow and then Samir can cover dedicated/private differences.
[01:10] Samir Patel: For technical folks: hosted API gives you fastest time-to-first-token — no infra changes. Dedicated gives predictable throughput (reserved GPU pools) and Private gives VPC/on-prem where the control plane is customer-managed.
[01:30] Mark Davies: When you say "first token in under 10 minutes" — what's the usual blocker? onboarding, or model pull times?
[01:40] Samir Patel: Usually the blocker is org setup + API key rotation — model pull is handled by our runtime; for small tests you hit token generation almost immediately. for larger model downloads with private deployments, kernel warmup/quantized model pulls add time.
[02:00] Lena Ortiz: For our pilot we expect bursts of traffic with short 64-128 token responses. typical qps target is 30-50 qps. how does Redwood handle batching vs latency in that regime?
[02:20] Samir Patel: We do continuous batching but it is workload-aware — for short seqs we favor low-latency kernels and smaller batch windows. you can set latency SLOs and routing policies. there's a cost/latency dial — increase batching to save tokens, decrease to meet p95 latency.
[02:45] Mark Davies: Any published perf numbers for 64 token responses on an A100-ish class node?
[02:54] Samir Patel: We publish profiles in the model catalog; rough ballpark — hosted endpoints on our optimized runtime hit ~60-100ms per request for 64 tokens on some open models, but depends on model size and quantization. I'll send the specific perf sheet.
[03:15] Priya Singh: On the security side — is Redwood SOC 2 certified? who manages keys if we use private?
[03:25] Maya Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II. for hosted we can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and we provide audit logs; for Private you manage keys (HSM/KMS) in your environment. Samir will drop the security bundle after this.
[03:40] Lena Ortiz: Good. and SSO? we use Okta.
[03:45] Samir Patel: SSO via SAML / OIDC is supported for Console accounts. RBAC is available. We'll include SSO setup notes.
[03:55] Maya Chen: Quick qualifier: what's the timeline for a pilot? are you looking to ship prod by end of quarter?
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: We want a small pilot in 4-6 weeks if possible. Must have SOC2/some VPC controls for customer data.
[04:12] Maya Chen: That sounds reasonable. typical path: self-serve quickstart with free credits to validate functionality, then a short POC where we can spin up Dedicated if you need committed capacity, or Private for VPC/on-prem.
[04:28] Mark Davies: If we start with hosted quickstart, how disruptive is it to move to Dedicated later?
[04:34] Samir Patel: Minimal from the API surface — same endpoints, same model catalog. routing and capacity change under the hood. you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts.
[04:48] Mark Davies: Cool. pricing — what's the expected per-token cost difference between hosted and dedicated?
[04:56] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract so unit cost typically drops but requires commit. we'll send indicative pricing in the follow-up.
[05:10] Lena Ortiz: Are there any limitations on data retention for hosted? we need to confirm retention and whether logs can be disabled.
[05:20] Samir Patel: By default we retain logs for diagnostics; enterprise customers can configure retention and opt out of storing user-generated content. we'll include the retention policy in the security bundle.
[05:35] Priya Singh: Do you support bringing-your-own-models or custom fine-tuning?
[05:42] Samir Patel: We support model variants and onboarding custom models in Dedicated/Private. hosted supports a curated catalog — if you need fine-tuning, we have integrations and recommendations. for many teams the quickest path is using our catalog in hosted to start.
[06:00] Mark Davies: For the quickstart, do we get actual API keys and credits that we can use from our CI?
[06:07] Maya Chen: Yes — we can provision a trial org with credits, you get API keys, and a quickstart guide shows SDK examples. it's designed to be CI-friendly.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: Great. what's the typical success criteria you see to flip from trial to POC?
[06:26] Maya Chen: Usually: 1) integrates with minimal engineering effort; 2) meets p95 latency targets for sample flows; 3) cost projections look reasonable; 4) security & compliance checks pass.
[06:40] Mark Davies: For latency testing — can we run synthetic benchmarks from our region? we'd like to see p95 from our US-east infra.
[06:48] Samir Patel: Absolutely. we can run bench runs from our hosted endpoints and also replicate on Dedicated if you want identical infra. If you provide sample payloads I'll run a bench and share results.
[07:05] Priya Singh: About VPC peering — if we need Private, do you support VPC peering or private link?
[07:13] Samir Patel: We support VPC peering and direct connect options depending on region; details will be in the infra notes we'll send.
[07:25] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas migrating from hosted to private?
[07:29] Samir Patel: Main things: model weights fetch time and kernel compatibility for some quantized builds; also networking setup. We run compatibility checks and provide preflight runbooks.
[07:45] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — do you have engineers who will run the bench and own the POC?
[07:50] Mark Davies: I'll own the bench, Priya will own security signoff, and Lena will be exec sponsor.
[08:00] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll send the quickstart link and credits and Samir will send the security bundle.
[08:08] Mark Davies: On SDKs — we use Python primarily. is there official SDK and quick examples for streaming?
[08:15] Samir Patel: Yes, we have Python and JS SDKs, streaming responses, function/tool calling patterns, and examples in the quickstart repo. sometimes the auto-transcript spells it "Redwood QuickStart" or "redwood quick star" — but it's the same thing.
[08:32] Lena Ortiz: We also want to validate cost at 50 qps for 8 hour windows. can you help model that?
[08:40] Maya Chen: yes, we'll ask for your expected token per request distribution and provide a cost projection sheet.
[08:48] Priya Singh: A question on logs: are audit logs immutable and exportable to our SIEM?
[08:54] Samir Patel: Audit logs are exportable. you can stream them to your logging infra or we can push to S3; immutability depends on retention policy but we support append-only storage options for compliance customers.
[09:10] Mark Davies: competitive question — any customers who moved from Anthropic/OpenAI to Redwood for infra reasons?
[09:18] Maya Chen: yes, a few infra-first customers migrated for predictable latency and cost controls; I'll include anonymized case notes.
[09:28] Lena Ortiz: that's helpful.
[09:32] Maya Chen: Any other blockers we should know about?
[09:36] Priya Singh: For security, we'd like to review the SOC2 report and the network diagram showing where keys live.
[09:44] Samir Patel: we'll include SOC2 Type II and the architecture diagram, plus KMS notes.
[09:50] Mark Davies: timeline recap — we aim to start a hosted quickstart this week and run bench next week. Does that work?
[09:58] Maya Chen: yes. I'll provision credits today and send the quickstart guide. Samir can schedule the bench.
[10:06] Lena Ortiz: Good. any risks in the quickstart that would prevent benching?
[10:12] Samir Patel: No major risks. if your sample payloads are heavy (long sequences), we might need to tweak batch settings. but for 64-128 tokens it's straightforward.
[10:28] Mark Davies: For monitoring — do you expose per-route latency and token costs?
[10:34] Samir Patel: Yes — Console gives per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and traces.
[10:42] Priya Singh: One more on compliance: do you support data residency in EU?
[10:48] Maya Chen: Yes, we have hosted regions in EU and can pin region routing for data residency. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[11:00] Lena Ortiz: ok, next steps and owners?
[11:03] Maya Chen: I'll recap at the end.
[11:06] Samir Patel: quick note — I'll include a short checklist for moving from hosted to Dedicated to make migration predictable.
[11:12] Maya Chen: Great. let's move into a short Q&A and then recap.
[11:25] [Q&A covers a few quick clarifications — transcript omitted for brevity]

[35:00] Maya Chen: (recap) Action items: Maya to provision trial org + credits and send quickstart; Samir to send SOC2 + infra diagram + perf sheet; Mark to provide sample workload. We tentatively schedule bench next Tue.
[35:20] Mark Davies: confirmed — I'll send sample payloads by Monday.
[35:30] Priya Singh: I'll review SOC2 once it's in.
[35:40] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, appreciate the clear path.
[35:48] Maya Chen: thanks all — expect emails from me and Samir within 24 hours.
[36:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains some minor transcription artifacts (names, product casing). References: quickstart repo link (sent in followup), security bundle (zip), perf spreadsheet (link).
